title: Fun & Games
description: The title track of the Raleigh band's 1989 album — hushed acoustic verses that burst into a fist-pumping power-pop chorus, pure Southern jangle with extra amplifier buzz.

pops.text: The Connells formed in Raleigh, North Carolina, in 1984 — brothers Mike and David Connell with singer Doug MacMillan out front.
This is the title track of their third album Fun & Games, released February 14, 1989, on TVT Records.
The song was co-written by MacMillan and Mike Connell — MacMillan was taking a bigger songwriting role on this record.
Producer Gary Smith, known for his work with the Pixies and Throwing Muses, produced the album.
The album reached #168 on the Billboard 200 — college radio, not Top 40, was the Connells' home turf.
Hear the pivot: a quiet, pastoral opening verse gives way to a big, anthemic, almost arena-sized chorus.
George Huntley, the band's other guitarist, contributes backing vocals here — he wrote album cuts like 'Sal' and 'Motel' himself.
The Connells were part of the Southern jangle-pop wave that followed in R.E.M.'s wake, alongside bands like Let's Active.
Four years later they'd score their biggest hit, ''74–'75' — a European smash from the album Ring in 1993.
The band kept going for decades and returned in 2021 with Steadman's Wake, their first album in 20 years.

title: Heaven Knows
description: Plant's sleek late-'80s comeback single from Now and Zen — glossy synths, a No. 1 rock-chart run, and a guitar solo smuggled in by Jimmy Page himself.

pops.text: Released January 18, 1988, as the first single from Plant's fourth solo album, Now and Zen.
It was written by keyboard player Phil Johnstone and David Barratt — not by Plant himself.
It hit No. 1 on Billboard's Album Rock Tracks chart — Plant's third No. 1 on that chart — and No. 33 in the UK.
That's Jimmy Page playing the guitar solo — a Led Zeppelin reunion in miniature, years before Page & Plant formally teamed up.
Page also guested on the album track 'Tall Cool One,' which cheekily sampled old Zeppelin riffs.
Now and Zen was Plant's deliberate embrace of modern production — keyboards and samples front and centre after years of him resisting Zeppelin nostalgia.
The B-side was 'Walking Towards Paradise,' a track that didn't make the album.
Plant co-produced the record with Tim Palmer and Phil Johnstone.
The album went triple platinum in the US — his biggest-selling solo record.
The video was a staple of late-'80s MTV, all moody lighting to match the song's sleek, nocturnal groove.

title: Angel
description: A feather-light Like a Virgin single with a famous quirk: no proper music video was ever filmed — Sire cut a montage of her earlier clips for the UK instead.

pops.text: Written by Madonna and Stephen Bray, and produced by Nile Rodgers of Chic.
Released April 10, 1985, as the third single from her second album, Like a Virgin (1984).
Madonna said the lyric came from a girlhood feeling: a girl in a depression is saved by an angel and falls madly in love with him.
It peaked at No. 5 on the Billboard Hot 100 — her fifth straight Top 5 single, a run no female artist had matched at that point.
No official video was filmed — Madonna already had so many clips in rotation that Warner Bros. scrapped the plan.
For the UK, Sire assembled a promo clip from pieces of 'Burning Up,' 'Borderline,' 'Lucky Star,' 'Like a Virgin' and 'Material Girl.'
In the US, the 12-inch paired 'Angel' with 'Into the Groove' — the double-sided release topped Billboard's dance sales chart.
Madonna performed it only on one tour: The Virgin Tour in 1985 — then essentially retired it live.
Oddly, it was left off her major hits compilations for years, a fan sore point finally eased by later reissues.
A remastered dance-remix edit of 'Angel' was released digitally on April 10, 2024 — exactly 39 years after the single.

title: CTI
description: Denver funk outfit Analog Son's opening salvo from Funky Mother — a jazzy organ-and-wah homage to Creed Taylor's legendary CTI label, cut live-in-the-room style.

pops.text: Analog Son is a Denver funk project founded by guitarist Jordan Linit and bassist Josh Fairman of SunSquabi.
The title is a tribute: CTI was Creed Taylor's 1970s label, home to George Benson, Herbie Hancock and Grover Washington Jr.
This was released as a 2018 single ahead of the album Funky Mother, then became the album's opening track.
Funky Mother was the band's fourth album and their first for Color Red, the label founded by Eddie Roberts of The New Mastersounds — who also produced it.
That's Eric Luba's organ driving the tune — reviewers singled out his jam as the track's engine.
Linit's wah-wah guitar rides on top, aiming squarely for an authentic 1970s jazz-funk feel.
The core band here: George Horn on drums, Michael Chiesa on tenor sax, Gabe Mervine on trumpet and Will Trask on percussion.
All About Jazz called it probably the band's jazziest jazz-funk song to that point.
The album was recorded as a live session — the band played together in the room rather than stacking overdubs.
Funky Mother's release party was September 28, 2018, at Cervantes' in Denver, with the Color Red All-Stars on the bill.

title: Have You Ever Seen The Rain
description: John Fogerty's deceptively sunny lament from Pendulum — really about Creedence falling apart at their peak — paired with the official 2018 video shot for the band's 50th anniversary.

pops.text: Written by John Fogerty and released on Pendulum in December 1970; the single followed in January 1971 and peaked at No. 8 in the US.
Despite the weather imagery, Fogerty has said it's about the band itself — success raining down while Creedence was breaking up inside.
The 'rain coming down on a sunny day' was his image for that contradiction: everything looks bright, something is still wrong.
Tom Fogerty, John's brother, left the band weeks after this single's release — the fracture the song saw coming.
Pendulum was CCR's sixth album in just over two years — an astonishing run of productivity.
It was the only CCR album with no cover songs — every track is a Fogerty original.
Fogerty played keyboards and saxophone on Pendulum, expanding the band's stripped-down sound.
This official video arrived in 2018 for CCR's 50th anniversary, directed by Laurence Jacobs and starring Jack Quaid and Erin Moriarty.
The video follows three friends on a last day together in Montana before one of them moves away.
The song has been covered by everyone from Rod Stewart to Willie Nelson and Bonnie Tyler — a standard now, rain and all.

title: Back to Land
description: The title track of the San Francisco psych quartet's 2013 album — their first record conceived after frontman Ripley Johnson's move to Oregon, and a slightly clearer, spacier Shjips voyage.

pops.text: Wooden Shjips are a psychedelic rock quartet formed in San Francisco, led by guitarist Ripley Johnson, also of Moon Duo.
Back to Land, released November 2013 on Thrill Jockey, was their fourth studio album, following 2011's West.
It was the first Wooden Shjips record conceived outside San Francisco — Johnson and drummer Omar Ahsanuddin had relocated to Oregon.
The album was recorded over 11 days at Jackpot! Recording Studio in Portland, engineered by Kendra Lynn and mixed by Larry Crane.
The official video was directed and produced by Benjael Halfmaderholz of Hylas Film.
The band's method is minimalism as hypnosis: locked, repetitive grooves, fuzzed organ from Nash Whalen, and Johnson's echoing guitar.
Johnson has said the nautically-themed band name nods to Crosby, Stills, Nash & Young's 'Wooden Ships' — with a deliberately trippy spelling.
Reviewers called Back to Land some of the band's most detailed and spacious recording — same trance, clearer air.
The album's limited vinyl came in a die-cut gatefold sleeve with a bonus 7-inch.
Johnson formed Moon Duo with Sanae Yamada as a Shjips side project — by Back to Land, both bands were running in parallel.

title: Lovesong
description: Robert Smith's wedding present to his wife Mary — the plainest, warmest song on the vast, dark Disintegration, filmed by Tim Pope inside a fake cave because the real one said no.

pops.text: Robert Smith wrote this as a wedding gift for his wife Mary Poole — they married in August 1988, after being together since they were teenagers.
Released August 21, 1989, as the third single from Disintegration, it became The Cure's biggest US hit, peaking at No. 2 on the Billboard Hot 100.
It was kept off No. 1 in America by Janet Jackson's 'Miss You Much.'
Director Tim Pope wanted to film the video in Cheddar Gorge cave in Somerset, couldn't get permission, and rebuilt the cave in a London studio instead.
Keyboardist Roger O'Donnell wrote the B-side, 'Fear of Ghosts.'
Smith has said Disintegration needed this song — without one straightforward love song, the album's darkness would have been dishonest.
The bassline is Simon Gallup's — a simple, circling figure the whole song floats on.
Adele covered it on her album 21 in 2011, introducing the song to a new generation; 311 had earlier taken it into the US Top 10 in 2004.
Smith and Mary met at school at 14 — he has said she is the subject of his love songs across the whole catalogue.
Disintegration is widely ranked among the greatest albums of the 1980s — and this is its beating heart.

title: Call Me
description: The breakthrough single from the Birmingham, Alabama soul revivalists' debut Half the City — Paul Janeway's rafter-raising voice in Jen West's official video.

pops.text: St. Paul & The Broken Bones formed in Birmingham, Alabama, in 2011 — singer Paul Janeway and bassist Jesse Phillips are the founding core.
Janeway grew up singing in church and was training to be a chef — and had worked as a mechanic — before the band took off.
'Call Me' is from their debut album Half the City, released in February 2014 on Single Lock Records.
The official video was directed by Jen West.
The band's name plays on Janeway's nickname — friends called the preacher-voiced singer 'St. Paul.'
Janeway's stage style — gold shoes, capes, crawling across the floor — channels Otis Redding and James Brown, his twin heroes.
The song landed in the 2015 film Fifty Shades of Grey, a huge exposure boost for a debut-album track.
Their Letterman performance of this song in January 2015 became a word-of-mouth sensation — the host demanded they keep playing.
Half the City was recorded in Muscle Shoals, Alabama, at FAME Studios' orbit — the town where Aretha and Otis cut classics.
The album was produced by Ben Tanner of Alabama Shakes, another Alabama act riding the soul-revival wave.

title: Bring It On Home to Me
description: Cooke's pleading soul standard from 1962 — a call-and-response duet with a young Lou Rawls, released as the B-side of 'Having a Party' and bigger than the A-side ever dreamed.

pops.text: Written by Sam Cooke and released May 8, 1962, by RCA Victor — as the B-side of 'Having a Party.'
The call-and-response vocal answering Cooke is Lou Rawls, then a little-known singer Cooke had mentored since their gospel days in Chicago.
Cooke and Rawls had sung together in the Teenage Kings of Harmony and crossed paths in the Soul Stirrers' orbit — this record reunited them.
It peaked at No. 13 on the Billboard Hot 100 and No. 2 on the R&B chart — outrunning its own A-side's fame over time.
The song was produced by Hugo & Luigi, Cooke's RCA producers, with a light string arrangement behind an unusually raw vocal.
Rolling Stone ranked it among the 500 greatest songs of all time, and it entered the Grammy Hall of Fame.
The Animals took their cover to No. 7 in the UK in 1965; Van Morrison, Otis Redding and Aretha Franklin all recorded it too.
Its gospel bones show in the call-and-response structure — Cooke learned that trade singing lead with the Soul Stirrers through the 1950s.
Cooke wrote it while at the peak of his powers as both singer and businessman — he ran his own label, SAR Records, and publishing company.
Sam Cooke died in December 1964, just two and a half years after this release — he was 33.

title: Haggis Express
description: A full-throttle instrumental funk single from the Leeds horn institution's fifth album Stand Up For Love — deep-pocket drums, scratchy guitar, congas and a fiery Hammond solo.

pops.text: The Haggis Horns are a funk band from Leeds, England, built around one of the UK's most hired horn sections.
'Haggis Express' was the first single from their fifth studio album, Stand Up For Love, released May 22, 2020, on their own Haggis Records.
It's a pure instrumental — drums and bass deep in the pocket, scratchy funk guitar, Latin-fire congas and a Hammond organ solo.
Reviewers heard a 1970s cop-movie theme in it — Glide Magazine called it an ultra-funky instrumental built for dancing.
The Horns first appeared on record in 1999, guesting on The New Mastersounds' debut album — the Leeds funk scene is a small world.
As session players, members have recorded or toured with Mark Ronson, Amy Winehouse, Jamiroquai, John Legend & The Roots and Adele.
Trumpeter Malcolm Strachan is a Haggis Horns core member — he has also released solo albums on the band's own Haggis Records.
Their sound deliberately channels Kool & The Gang, Fred Wesley & The J.B.'s, The Meters and The Fatback Band.
Stand Up For Love was their most vocal-led album, with singer John McCallum on seven of nine tracks — which makes this instrumental the exception.
The band's name is a Scottish joke worn by Englishmen: haggis, plus horns, plus an endless series of haggis-titled instrumentals.

title: Hey Nineteen
description: Donald Fagen's sleek, queasy tale of a May-December date going nowhere — the No. 10 hit that opens side two of Gaucho, an album that took two years and a small army of session stars.

pops.text: From Gaucho, Steely Dan's seventh album, released November 21, 1980 — 'Hey Nineteen' peaked at No. 10 on the Billboard Hot 100.
Written by Donald Fagen and Walter Becker, it's sung from the view of an older man realising a 19-year-old date has never heard of Aretha Franklin.
The chorus name-checks 'the Cuervo Gold' — Becker used to perform a spoken live intro riffing on the tequila and the song's ageing narrator.
Gaucho took roughly two years to make and used more than 40 session musicians — the peak of the Dan's perfectionist method.
The sessions were troubled: Becker was seriously injured when struck by a taxi in New York during recording.
Producer Gary Katz steered the album; engineers famously spent days on single drum sounds.
The credits are peak session-era Dan: producer Gary Katz, and backing vocalists including Patti Austin, Frank Floyd and Zack Sanders.
The album's original sessions produced an entire lost song, 'The Second Arrangement,' accidentally erased by an engineer — Dan lore's most famous mishap.
Gaucho won the Grammy for Best Engineered Album, and in 1981 effectively ended the band's first era — they didn't tour or record together again for over a decade.
Steely Dan were never a video band — this track's visuals in the MTV era were essentially nil; the record lived on FM radio instead.

title: Kick That Hustle
description: A two-minute horn-fanfare funk blast from the UK veterans' Abbey Road Masters sessions — library music cut live at Abbey Road that proved too good to stay in the vault.

pops.text: Speedometer are a British funk and soul band led by guitarist Leigh Gracie, playing heavy funk since the late 1990s.
'Kick That Hustle' comes from Abbey Road Masters: The Funk Sessions, released March 31, 2023.
The sessions were recorded live at Abbey Road Studios in London — the band playing as an eight-piece in the room.
Universal Music commissioned the recordings for its Abbey Road Masters library label, originally as music for TV and film use.
The track runs just 2:10 — library cuts are built short, sharp and instantly usable.
It opens with a horn fanfare, drops into a guitar-bass-drums groove, then the horns kick straight back in — a James Brown-style construction.
Demand from fans led to a limited vinyl release of the sessions — just 250 copies pressed for The Funk & Soul Sessions LP.
The combined LP pairs the funk instrumentals with vocal soul tracks featuring SheZar and Angelo Starr — younger brother of Edwin Starr.
Speedometer marked their 25th anniversary around these releases, a quarter-century as UK funk's workhorses.
Before Abbey Road called, Speedometer had spent years building their reputation on the UK funk circuit with a run of albums for Freestyle Records.

title: Save Tonight
description: The Swedish singer-songwriter's one immortal hit — four chords, one last night together, and a black-and-white Stockholm video in which Cherry plays every character on the street.

pops.text: Released October 7, 1997, as the lead single from Eagle-Eye Cherry's debut album Desireless.
Eagle-Eye is the son of American jazz trumpeter Don Cherry and Swedish artist Monika Karlsson — and half-brother of singer Neneh Cherry.
He wrote 'Save Tonight' late in the album sessions and has said he knew immediately it was special.
It peaked at No. 5 on the Billboard Hot 100 in early 1999 — more than a year after its Swedish release — and No. 6 in the UK.
The black-and-white video was shot on the streets of Stockholm, with Cherry playing every role: the lover, a butcher, a truck driver, a busker.
Before music, Cherry acted — he studied at the School of Performing Arts in New York and appeared on The Cosby Show as a teenager.
The song is built on a simple four-chord loop that never changes from first verse to final chorus — part of why it lodges in the brain.
Desireless was recorded largely in Cherry's bedroom studio in Stockholm, on acoustic guitar, after he moved back from New York.
Desireless was released in Sweden in 1997 and rolled out internationally through 1998 — the single's slow climb mirrored the album's.
It remains one of the defining one-hit wonders of the late 1990s — and he has said he has made his peace with that completely.

title: Be Yourself
description: The title track of the Leeds funk quartet's second album — Eddie Roberts' guitar, a chugging organ groove, and the Meters-and-Booker T. blueprint played with total conviction.

pops.text: The New Mastersounds formed in Leeds, England, in February 1999, founded by guitarist Eddie Roberts.
'Be Yourself' is the title track of their second album, released November 3, 2003, on One Note Records.
Roberts has described the band's blueprint plainly: the instrumental sound of The Meters and Booker T. & The M.G.'s.
The band's debut, Keb Darge Presents The New Mastersounds (2001), was championed by legendary funk DJ Keb Darge, who produced their first single 'One Note Brown.'
This album features a then little-known Leeds singer named Corinne Bailey Rae — three years before her own Grammy-winning solo breakthrough.
Bailey Rae sings 'Your Love Is Mine' on this record — later a hit single for the band in 2006.
The classic quartet sound: Roberts' guitar, Joe Tatton's organ and piano, Pete Shand's bass and Simon Allen's drums.
Gilles Peterson playlisted their early tracks, and their debut was remixed by Kenny Dope and sampled by DJ Shadow's circle.
The Be Yourself album runs 14 tracks in about 51 minutes — dancefloor funk with no filler philosophy.
The New Mastersounds later relocated their centre of gravity to the US, touring relentlessly and recording in New Orleans and Nashville.

title: Livin' Thing
description: Jeff Lynne's soaring single from A New World Record — flamenco-tinged strings, a love-gone lyric Lynne traced to a bout of food poisoning, and ELO's first UK Top 5 hit of the era.

pops.text: Written and produced by Jeff Lynne for A New World Record, released as a single in October 1976.
It reached No. 4 in the UK and No. 13 on the Billboard Hot 100 — one of four hit singles from the album.
Lynne has said the lyric about love slipping away had an unglamorous spark: he first drafted its 'sailing away' melancholy while ill with food poisoning in Spain.
The intro's Spanish-flavoured flourishes come from the band's three-man string section — violinists Mik Kaminski and the cellists Hugh McDowell and Melvyn Gale.
ELO's classic seven-piece lineup is all here: Lynne, drummer Bev Bevan, bassist Kelly Groucutt, keyboardist Richard Tandy and the strings.
A New World Record was recorded at Musicland Studios in Munich — the same rooms Queen and Led Zeppelin used.
The album was ELO's commercial breakthrough in America, eventually certified platinum.
The official video is a straight performance clip of the band with its full string section — ELO's orchestral-pop concept made visible.
Groucutt, who joined in 1974, shares backing vocals throughout — his harmony blend with Lynne defines the mid-'70s ELO sound.
The song got a second life soundtracking the finale of the 1997 film Boogie Nights — 'it's a livin' thing' over the credits.
